unit: codeql (plan move M4): measure the CodeQL quality suites before any setup change
host_bounds: 48 CPUs, about 77 GiB available at start; every CodeQL process ran with --threads=8 --ram=12288 and the three language pipelines ran in parallel. Nothing was installed host-wide: the bundle was extracted into the unit's scratch directory <dl>, outside the checkout.

placeholders.<dl>: the unit's scratch download directory, outside every repository
placeholders.<worktree>: the unit's owned git worktree at measured_commit

suites_run.code-scanning: <lang>-code-scanning.qls, the default suite (what default setup runs)
suites_run.code-quality: <lang>-code-quality.qls (code-quality-selectors.yml: problem or path-problem, precision high or very-high, tag quality)
suites_run.security-and-quality: <lang>-security-and-quality.qls (python and javascript: security-and-frozen-quality-selectors.yml plus an explicit list of 122 and 102 quality query ids; actions: security-and-quality-selectors.yml)
suites_run.security-extended: <lang>-security-extended.qls, the suite default setup calls Extended (run to measure the deferred fallback)

steps_note: The first twelve steps ran through run.sh (three language pipelines in parallel); the three security-extended steps ran afterwards on the same databases, invoked as ./codeql/codeql from <dl>. Stderr lines that mention errors or warnings are query names (SyntaxError.bqrs, EncodingError.bqrs, UnhandledErrorInStreamPipeline.bqrs) and 'Interpreting' progress lines, not failures.

run_integrity.claim: Every step of the recorded run exited 0, so the run.sh defect found in review did not affect these counts. That run.sh waited with a bare `wait`, which returns zero whatever the jobs returned (bash(1), wait), and its analysis loop continued after a failed step, so a replay could record ALL DONE with missing results.
run_integrity.run_sh_used: sha256 3346ee74e9b42b9bcac8019bbc30e62eb41614e48d8c7371c5fdc3af40974b9a, 1838 bytes: run.sh as first committed (f137ede7), byte-identical to the retained <dl>/run.sh
records: <dl>/steps.tsv has 15 step lines, each with exit code 0 in its fourth column: the twelve run.sh steps, then 'ALL DONE 2026-09-28T02:08:09Z', then the three security-extended steps. step() records each command's own exit status, so this column is direct evidence; the defect was only in how run.sh acted on those statuses.
<dl>/logs/create-python.err, create-javascript.err and create-actions.err each end with 'Successfully created database at <dl>/db/<language>.'
Each of the 12 <dl>/logs/analyze-<language>-<suite>.err files ends with 'Exporting results to SARIF...' and 'Exported results to SARIF (<n>ms).'
The 12 files in <dl>/sarif hash to sarif_sha256.local, hold the result counts in counts.json, and record invocations[0].executionSuccessful true with no error-level toolExecutionNotifications.
run_integrity.fix: run.sh now stops a language pipeline at its first failed step and waits on each pipeline's PID. It writes ALL DONE and exits 0 only when all three pipelines succeed; otherwise it appends a FAILED line naming them and exits 1. The CodeQL argv is unchanged. In a replay with a stub codeql that returns 23, the old script exited 0 with ALL DONE when all three database creations failed and the new one exited 1 with FAILED.
run_integrity.class: our-integration (a reading of the retained <dl> records; the fix and the stub replay concern local glue, not CodeQL)

sarif_sha256.why_not_committed: CodeQL SARIF records the absolute source root (originalUriBaseIds) and the live SARIF the runner's; the files stay in <dl> and only their hashes and derived counts are published.

alert_states.note: The 17 live default-suite results at measured_commit (16 python, 1 javascript-typescript) belong to dismissed alerts. Under security-and-quality, the 1,056 python and 189 javascript-typescript results beyond the default suite would be new alerts.

live_default_setup.flag_differences: Default setup's database init also passed --calculate-language-specific-baseline, --sublanguage-file-coverage, --extractor-include-aliases, --codescanning-config and --overlay-base, and --build-mode=none for actions; the local run passed none of these. The default-suite results still matched exactly (parity below).

parity.claim: The local default-suite (code-scanning) SARIF equals the live default-setup SARIF at the same commit, as multisets of (rule id, path, start line, start column), for python (16 = 16 results, 43 = 43 rules), javascript-typescript (1 = 1, 87 = 87) and actions (0 = 0, 17 = 17).
parity.vacuity: Actions parity is vacuous for results (0 = 0); only its rule set (17 = 17, same ids) is a non-vacuous match.
parity.negative_control: The same comparator on a mismatched pair (local python code-quality SARIF against the live python SARIF) reports identical=false, same_rule_ids=false, 979 local-only results.

self_check.claim: The four receipt scripts add no CodeQL results of their own: a python database built from a scratch copy of only these files gives 0 results under code-scanning, code-quality and security-and-quality (CodeQL 2.27.1, --build-mode=none).
self_check.negative_control: The same code-quality check on a copy of triage.py with a planted unused `import shutil` and an unclosed `open(path).read()` reports 2 results (py/unused-import, py/file-not-closed).

upstream-unchanged: CodeQL CLI 2.27.1 and its bundled query packs ran unchanged, with the bundle's own suite files; the counts in counts.json are their SARIF output.

Bundle integrity and release membership were checked with GitHub's native verifiers (release asset digest, published checksum asset, gh release verify-asset), each with a failing negative control, before the CLI ran.
our-integration: run.sh, summarize_sarif.py, sample_alerts.py and triage.py are thin glue around the upstream CLI and the SARIF 2.1.0 format: counts, lane split (docs/lanes.md read literally), the parity comparison and its negative control, the seeded stratified draw, population heuristics and the volume-weighted extrapolation.
The 26 verdicts in triage_verdicts.json are this unit's reading of the source, recorded with file:line reasons; they are not an upstream or independent verdict.
The parity target is GitHub's own default-setup analysis and SARIF for the same commit (a live platform record that was read, not rerun).
live-run-pending: No advanced-setup workflow and no Extended default-setup analysis ran on GitHub.
How merge protection would treat new quality or Extended alerts on a real pull request is taken from GitHub's documentation, not observed on a pull request.
csharp, go and rust were not analysed locally; only their live default-suite analyses (0 results each) were read.

code-scanning alerts (severity and security severity; alerts in pull requests; non-application-code labels), CodeQL query suites, workflow configuration options, rulesets 'Require code scanning results', set code scanning merge protection, GitHub Code Quality (availability and billing)

limitations: One commit and one host; the counts change with the code and with the CodeQL version.

Triage covers one alert per sampled rule (20) plus a 6-alert supplement; the volume-weighted figures extrapolate each sampled verdict to its rule's other results, and population heuristics support but do not replace per-result verdicts.
Actions has no quality coverage at CodeQL 2.27.1: actions-code-quality.qls selects 0 queries. That is missing coverage, not a clean result.

The lane split applies docs/lanes.md literally: evidence/artifacts/ and non-trading scripts/ are unassigned there and reported as unlisted, although the seven JavaScript pages under evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/us-equities__* serve the trading lane in intent (lanes.md names only the blueprints/ form of that glob).
Raw SARIF, databases and logs stay in <dl> (they record absolute paths); published values are derived counts, hashes and repository-relative locations.
